_comment: Single source of truth for PatchStorage listing metadata. One entry per plugin short-name (matches the LV2 URI suffix and the <name>.lv2 bundle). generate_metadata.py renders this into the uploader's plugins.json (source/donate/license/categories/tags) plus a LISTINGS.md per target; split_bundle.py injects 'long' into each bundle TTL as rdfs:comment, which is what PatchStorage shows as the listing description. Source/donate links live ONLY in the structured source_code_url/donate_url fields (which become the profile/listing buttons) — NOT repeated in the description body. 'nam' marks the NAM-capable plugins: NAM is present on linux-amd64 + rpi-aarch64 and hidden on patchbox-os-arm32.

amp.title: Hex Chain Amp
amp.short: Six original guitar-amp voicings + a modeled power-amp stage, plus a NAM loader for your own captures.
amp.long:
A complete guitar amp in one plugin. Six original preamp voicings run from sparkling clean to saturated high-gain, each feeding a modeled power-amp section — sag, presence, depth and resonance — for real cab-pushing feel rather than a flat distortion. A shared, footswitch-friendly tone stack keeps switching between voicings fast on stage.

On 64-bit/desktop targets a Neural (NAM) slot loads your own .nam amp captures to sit alongside the algorithmic models; on 32-bit (patchbox-os-arm32) NAM is omitted and the six models run on their own. Works standalone or as part of the Hex Chain suite / Hex Forge.

Free and open source (GPL-3). Amp names are original parodies and are not affiliated with any manufacturer.

cab.title: Hex Chain Cab
cab.short: Cabinet sim: load your own .wav IRs (and .nam rigs on 64-bit).
cab.long:
A convolution cabinet that loads your own .wav impulse responses, with low-cut, high-cut and dry/wet mix to dial the speaker voicing to taste. On 64-bit/desktop targets it can also load full-rig .nam captures that override the IR for amp-in-a-box tones. On 32-bit (patchbox-os-arm32) the NAM path is omitted; IR loading is unchanged.

Ships with an embedded default cab so it makes sound out of the box. Free and open source (GPL-3).

drive.title: Hex Chain Drive
drive.long:
Three original drive and boost voicings — Green Man, New Dawn and Dear Rodent Boy — covering transparent clean boost, mid-pushed overdrive and tight, focused gain, each with level and mix. Stack them in front of the Hex Chain Amp or your own rig.

On 64-bit/desktop targets a Neural (NAM) slot runs your own .nam pedal captures alongside the algorithmic voicings; on 32-bit (patchbox-os-arm32) NAM is omitted. Free and open source (GPL-3). Names are original parodies and are not affiliated with any manufacturer.

fuzz.title: Hex Chain Fuzz
fuzz.short: Multi-era Muff-style fuzz + germanium Tone Bender voicing.
fuzz.long:
A multi-era big-muff-style fuzz with several voicings, plus a component-accurate germanium Tone Bender MkII model. Oversampled for clean, defined high-gain without the aliasing fizz that plagues naive digital fuzz — from creamy sustain to spitty vintage grit.

Works standalone or in the Hex Chain suite. Free and open source (GPL-3). Names are original parodies and are not affiliated with any manufacturer.

nail.title: Hex Chain Nail
nail.short: Five-mode industrial distortion: fuzz, resonant filter, bitcrush, cab re-amp, ring-mod.
nail.long:
An industrial distortion block with five distinct topologies — each its own circuit, not one voicing knob: Broke (crude digital hard-clip with sample-rate decimation + bit-reduction), Dahnward (scooped high-gain preamp into a sweepable resonant band-pass), Delicate (a Swollen-Pickle-leaning big-muff), Con Molars (a bright clip re-amped through a fixed miked-speaker voicing) and Yo, Hey Adrian! (a high-sustain clip into a switchable ring modulator). Controls: Mode, Drive, Filter, Texture, Level, plus a Ring Mod toggle for the Yo, Hey Adrian! mode. Oversampled; works standalone or in the Hex Chain suite.

Amp pairing: some modes and settings work into a clean amp or DI; the higher-gain settings generally want a driven amp — a JCM 800-style Marshall works. Free and open source (GPL-3). Names are original and are not affiliated with any artist or manufacturer.

gate.title: Hex Chain Gate
gate.short: Low-CPU noise gate for high-gain rigs.
gate.long:
A clean, low-CPU noise gate with threshold and timing controls — tames hum and hiss in front of or after high-gain amps without chopping your sustain. Runs comfortably on every target including 32-bit Pi.

Free and open source (GPL-3).

comp.title: Hex Chain Compressor
comp.long:
A musical, low-CPU compressor for evening out picking dynamics and adding sustain — equally at home on guitar and bass, in front of a dirt pedal or across a clean signal. Runs on every target including 32-bit Pi.

Free and open source (GPL-3).

modfx.title: Hex Chain Modulation
modfx.short: Chorus / flanger / phaser in one block.
modfx.long:
A modulation block with chorus, flanger and phaser voicings and a unity-gain wet/dry mix, so engaging it never drops your level. Light on CPU; runs on every target including 32-bit Pi.

Free and open source (GPL-3).

delay.title: Hex Chain Delay
delay.long:
A delay block spanning clean digital, tape (wow/flutter), a multi-head rotary echo and a dual-delay 'Seraph' mode with pattern, ducking and modulation. Unity-gain mix so engaging it never drops your level.

Free and open source (GPL-3).

reverb.title: Hex Chain Reverb
reverb.long:
A smooth plate reverb with size, tone and mix and a unity-gain wet/dry blend so engaging it never drops your level — from a tight room to long, lush ambience. Heavier than the light effects but fine on Pi 4/5; usable on 32-bit Pi with headroom in mind.

Free and open source (GPL-3).

utility.title: Hex Chain Input Trim
utility.long:
A small but handy front-of-chain utility: clean gain trim, phase invert, a fixed 60 Hz hum-filter comb, and a single-coil→humbucker voicing. The voicing re-voices a single-coil pickup toward one of three target bridge humbuckers — '59 Bucker (warm vintage PAF), Norse Hammer (hot ceramic) or Modern Flux (active hi-fi) — with an Amount control (0 = bypass). Minimal CPU; runs on every target.

Free and open source (GPL-3). Names are original parodies and are not affiliated with any manufacturer.

hexforge.title: Hex Forge
hexforge.short: Your entire guitar rig — amp, cab, drives and effects — in one reorderable plugin with presets and footswitch recall.
hexforge.long:
Hex Forge is the flagship: the whole Hex Chain signal chain in a single plugin. Gate, compressor, drive, amp, cab, modulation, delay, reverb and an input-trim/utility block are all here — each independently bypassable and freely reorderable — so you build a complete board without patching nine separate plugins.

A built-in 8x4 preset/bank engine with A/B/C/D footswitch recall (and hold-both bank chords) lets you switch whole rigs hands-free. The factory pedalboard ships pre-wired, so the pi-Stomp footswitches work the moment you load it — no MIDI setup.

On 64-bit/desktop targets the amp, drive and cab slots load your own .nam captures; on 32-bit (patchbox-os-arm32) NAM is hidden and the algorithmic models are used. The heaviest plugin in the suite — best on Pi 4/5 and desktop. Free and open source (GPL-3).

wah.title: Hex Chain Wah
wah.long:
A wah with two modes: Auto, an envelope filter that sweeps with your picking dynamics, and Fixed, a parked "cocked-wah" midrange honk — so it works as a saved preset with no expression pedal needed. Resonance and range controls shape the vowel. Light on CPU; runs on every target including 32-bit Pi.

Works standalone or as part of the Hex Chain suite / Hex Forge. Free and open source (GPL-3).

octave.title: Hex Chain Octave
octave.long:
An analog-voiced octaver (OC-2 style): a flip-flop sub-octave plus a rectifier octave-up, blended with dry. Monophonic tracking — clean and singing on single notes, gnarlier on chords. Up, Sub and Dry controls set the blend. Light on CPU; runs on every target including 32-bit Pi.

Works standalone or as part of the Hex Chain suite / Hex Forge. Free and open source (GPL-3).
